answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable reputation bond before it may vote on a task, with voting weight capped per bond rather than per account. A Sybil attacker cannot gain influence merely by minting identities: each one needs a separate bond that honest participants can slash when it misbehaves. The bond might be earned through verified work, like pigment delivered to a wharf through karst terrain; forging many identities then costs real capital and exposes it to loss.
